## What this notebook does {.unnumbered}

A spheroid of radius 200 µm (about 1200 cells) is irradiated once with a
**polyenergetic carbon-ion beam** whose kinetic energy follows a **Gaussian
spectrum**. The **track-segment condition is switched off** (`track_seg = false`):
each particle loses energy along its path, so cells at different depths see
different energies and LET. The spheroid has a **radial oxygen profile**. After
irradiation, the **agent-based model** follows the spheroid for 96 h, and the
notebook analyses survival, cell fate and population dynamics.

It complements
[`example/spheroid.jl`](https://github.com/francescogcordoni/GSM2_Julia/blob/main/example/spheroid.jl)
(monoenergetic beam) and
[`example/spheroid_poly.jl`](https://github.com/francescogcordoni/GSM2_Julia/blob/main/example/spheroid_poly.jl)
(a few discrete energies). Render with
`quarto render example/features_walkthrough.qmd`.

## Setup

The utilities are included in `Main`, because the setup functions write their
results (the cell table, the irradiation conditions, …) as globals of `Main`;
`pull!` copies them into the notebook. All figures use the same margins, so that
axis labels stay inside the figure.

```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| output: false

import Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(homedir(), ".julia", "environments",
                      "v$(VERSION.major).$(VERSION.minor)"))

using Base.Threads, DataFrames, Distributions, Random, Printf
using Plots, StatsPlots, Statistics, StatsBase
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"          # headless GR

@eval Main begin
    using Base.Threads, Distributed, CSV, DataFrames, Distributions, Random
    using Plots, StatsPlots, Statistics, StatsBase, ProgressBars, ProgressMeter
    using GLM, Optim, LsqFit, JLD2, DelimitedFiles
    using InlineStrings, SparseArrays, Printf, CUDA
    using Statistics: mean
end
Base.include(Main, joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "src", "load_utilities.jl"))

using Main: GSM2, Ion, Irrad, AT
import Main: setup_GSM2!, setup_IonIrrad!, setup_cell_lattice!, setup_cell_population!,
             setup_irrad_conditions!, set_oxygen_diffusion!, calculate_beam_properties,
             load_stopping_power, table_for, let_at, validate_stopping,
             MC_dose_damage_poly!, domain_GSM2,
             set_fate_model!, set_checkpoint!, compute_times_domain!,
             run_simulation_abm!, _advance_idle!, print_phase_distribution

sp = load_stopping_power()
@eval Main sp = $sp

"Copy globals written into Main by the setup functions into this notebook."
function pull!(syms...)
    for s in syms
        isdefined(Main, s) && Core.eval(@__MODULE__, :($s = Main.$s))
    end
end

gr()
default(framestyle = :box, grid = true, gridalpha = 0.3, lw = 2,
        guidefontsize = 11, tickfontsize = 9, legendfontsize = 8,
        size = (800, 450), left_margin = 8Plots.mm, bottom_margin = 7Plots.mm,
        right_margin = 5Plots.mm, top_margin = 3Plots.mm,
        foreground_color_legend = nothing, background_color_legend = RGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.8))

const PHASES = ["G0", "G1", "S", "G2", "M"]
const PCOL   = Dict("G0" => :gray60, "G1" => :steelblue, "S" => :seagreen,
                    "G2" => :darkorange, "M" => :firebrick, "doomed" => :black)
println("Threads: ", nthreads())
```

## Parameters

```{julia}
#| label: parameters
#| output: false

# Beam: Gaussian energy spectrum
PARTICLE = "12C"
E_MEAN   = 20.0      # mean kinetic energy (MeV/u)
E_SIGMA  = 1.0       # standard deviation (MeV/u)
N_BINS   = 7         # energy bins
N_SIGMA  = 2.5       # spectrum truncated at ±N_SIGMA·σ
DOSE_GY  = 2.0       # dose at the entrance of the target (Gy)

# Geometry
TUMOR_RADIUS = 200.0;  R_CELL = 15.0;  X_BOX = 400.0;  X_VOXEL = 800.0
RD = 0.8;  RN = 7.2

# Physics and run options
TYPE_AT     = "KC"     # Kiefer–Chatterjee amorphous track
TRACK_SEG   = false    # energy loss along the path
TARGET_GEOM = "circle"; CALC_TYPE = "full"
NAT_APO     = 1e-10
T_FOLLOW    = 96       # h of agent-based dynamics after irradiation
SNAP_HOURS  = [0, 24, 48, 96]

# GSM² rates (h⁻¹), calibrated on phase-specific LQ data
gsm2_cycle = [GSM2(2.7805, 0.01287, 0.04030, RD, RN),   # G1 / G0
              GSM2(5.8401, 0.00589, 0.05794, RD, RN),   # S
              GSM2(1.7720, 0.02431, 5.705e-5, RD, RN),  # G2 / M
              GSM2(2.5657, 0.01481, 0.01266, RD, RN)]   # average

validate_stopping(sp, PARTICLE, parse(Int, match(r"\d+", PARTICLE).match))
Random.seed!(2026)
```

---

## The Gaussian energy spectrum

The kinetic energy follows $E \sim \mathcal{N}(\bar E, \sigma^2)$, truncated at
$\pm 2.5\sigma$ and split into `N_BINS` bins. Each bin $i$ is a monoenergetic
component with energy $E_i$ (the bin centre) and **fluence fraction** $w_i$ (its
Gaussian probability). Since a particle of bin $i$ deposits a dose proportional
to its LET, the prescribed dose fixes the total fluence:

$$
F_{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{D}{1.602\times10^{-9}\sum_i w_i\,\mathrm{LET}_i},
\qquad N_i = w_i\,F_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\pi R_{\mathrm{beam}}^2 .
$$

```{julia}
#| label: fig-spectrum
#| fig-cap: "Left: fluence fraction of each energy bin and the Gaussian spectrum. Right: LET of each bin at the entrance."

edges     = range(E_MEAN - N_SIGMA * E_SIGMA, E_MEAN + N_SIGMA * E_SIGMA; length = N_BINS + 1)
ENERGIES  = collect(0.5 .* (edges[1:end-1] .+ edges[2:end]))
W         = diff(cdf.(Normal(E_MEAN, E_SIGMA), collect(edges)));  W ./= sum(W)
PARTICLES = fill(PARTICLE, N_BINS)

LET_i = [let_at(table_for(sp, PARTICLE), E) for E in ENERGIES]
LET_F = sum(W .* LET_i)                         # fluence-averaged LET
LET_D = sum(W .* LET_i .^ 2) / sum(W .* LET_i)  # dose-averaged LET
@printf("Fluence-averaged LET %.1f keV/µm; dose-averaged LET %.1f keV/µm\n", LET_F, LET_D)

Eg = range(first(edges), last(edges); length = 200)
p1 = bar(ENERGIES, W; bar_width = step(edges), color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.6, label = "bins",
         xlabel = "Kinetic energy (MeV/u)", ylabel = "Fluence fraction")
plot!(p1, Eg, pdf.(Normal(E_MEAN, E_SIGMA), Eg) .* step(edges); color = :black, label = "Gaussian")
p2 = scatter(ENERGIES, LET_i; color = :firebrick, label = "", ms = 5,
             xlabel = "Kinetic energy (MeV/u)", ylabel = "LET (keV/µm)")
plot(p1, p2; layout = (1, 2), size = (900, 380))
```

## Spheroid, oxygen and irradiation conditions

```{julia}
#| label: build

setup_GSM2!(2.5657, 0.01481, 0.01266, RD, RN)
setup_IonIrrad!(DOSE_GY, ENERGIES, PARTICLES; type_AT = TYPE_AT)   # one Ion per energy bin

N_sideVox   = Int(floor(2 * X_BOX / X_VOXEL))
N_CellsSide = 2 * convert(Int64, floor(X_BOX / (2 * R_CELL)))
setup_cell_lattice!(TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, R_CELL, N_sideVox, N_CellsSide;
                    ParIrr = "false", track_seg = TRACK_SEG, full_cycle = true)
@eval Main begin
    tumor_radius = $TUMOR_RADIUS; X_voxel = $X_VOXEL; X_box = $X_BOX
end
setup_cell_population!(TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, R_CELL, N_sideVox, N_CellsSide,
                       gsm2_cycle[4]; ParIrr = "false")
pull!(:ion, :irrad, :LET, :cell_df, :df_center_x, :df_center_y, :at)

setup_irrad_conditions!(ion, irrad, TYPE_AT, cell_df, TRACK_SEG)   # energy loss per bin
pull!(:irrad_cond, :lets, :energies, :cell_df)

set_oxygen_diffusion!(cell_df; density = :radial)

alive0 = cell_df.is_cell .== 1
N_init = count(alive0)
cx, cy, cz = mean(cell_df.x[alive0]), mean(cell_df.y[alive0]), mean(cell_df.z[alive0])
cell_df.r = sqrt.((cell_df.x .- cx).^2 .+ (cell_df.y .- cy).^2 .+ (cell_df.z .- cz).^2)
println("Spheroid: $N_init cells")
print_phase_distribution(cell_df; label = "before irradiation")
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-oxygen
#| fig-cap: "Oxygen level of each cell as a function of its distance from the centre of the spheroid."

scatter(cell_df.r[alive0], cell_df.O[alive0]; ms = 2.5, msw = 0, alpha = 0.5, label = "",
        color = :steelblue, xlabel = "Distance from the centre (µm)", ylabel = "O₂ (%)")
```

---

## Energy loss along the path

With `track_seg = false`, the target is divided into layers perpendicular to the
beam, one per lattice plane. For each energy bin, the energy at the next layer is
$E_{i+1} = R^{-1}\!\left(R(E_i) - h\right)$, where $R(E)$ is the
continuous-slowing-down range from the stopping-power table and $R^{-1}$ its
inverse; the LET and the track parameters are recomputed at each layer. Empty
layers do not absorb, so the depth is measured from the surface of the spheroid.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-let-depth
#| fig-cap: "Kinetic energy (left) and LET (right) of each energy bin as a function of depth z. Dashed: entrance LET, i.e. the value used under the track-segment condition."

zs   = sort(unique(cell_df.z))
occ  = [any(alive0 .& (cell_df.z .== z)) for z in zs]    # layers that contain cells
cols = palette(:viridis, N_BINS)
pE = plot(xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "Energy (MeV/u)", legend = false)
pL = plot(xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "LET (keV/µm)", legend = :outerright)
for i in 1:N_BINS
    plot!(pE, zs[occ], energies[i][occ]; color = cols[i])
    plot!(pL, zs[occ], lets[i][occ]; color = cols[i], label = @sprintf("%.1f MeV/u", ENERGIES[i]))
    hline!(pL, [lets[i][findfirst(occ)]]; color = cols[i], ls = :dash, lw = 1, label = "")
end
plot(pE, pL; layout = (1, 2), size = (950, 380))
```

## Dose and DNA damage

```{julia}
#| label: dose

R_beam, _, _ = calculate_beam_properties(CALC_TYPE, TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, X_VOXEL, TUMOR_RADIUS)
F_tot     = DOSE_GY / (1.602e-9 * sum(W .* LET))     # particles / cm²
Npar_vect = round.(Int, W .* F_tot .* π .* R_beam^2 .* 1e-8)
println("Particles per energy bin: ", Npar_vect)

@time MC_dose_damage_poly!(ion, Npar_vect, R_beam, irrad_cond, cell_df,
                           df_center_x, df_center_y, at, gsm2_cycle, TYPE_AT, TRACK_SEG)
@printf("Mean cell dose %.2f Gy (prescribed at the entrance %.2f Gy)\n",
        mean(cell_df.dose_cell[alive0]), DOSE_GY)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-dose
#| fig-cap: "Left: distribution of the cell dose. Right: mean cell dose and mean number of sublethal lesions per cell as a function of depth: both rise as the particles slow down."

d   = cell_df[alive0, :]
d.X = [sum(v) for v in d.dam_X_dom]
g   = sort(combine(groupby(d, :z), :dose_cell => mean => :dose, :X => mean => :X), :z)

pD = histogram(d.dose_cell; bins = 40, normalize = :pdf, color = :firebrick, alpha = 0.6,
               label = "", xlabel = "Cell dose (Gy)", ylabel = "Probability density (Gy⁻¹)")
pZ = plot(g.z, g.dose; marker = :circle, ms = 3, color = :firebrick, label = "dose",
          xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "Mean cell dose (Gy)", legend = :topleft)
pX = twinx(pZ)
plot!(pX, g.z, g.X; marker = :diamond, ms = 3, color = :steelblue, label = "X lesions",
      ylabel = "Mean X lesions per cell", legend = :bottomright)
plot(pD, pZ; layout = (1, 2), size = (950, 380))
```

## Survival and fate

The survival probability of each cell is the exact GSM² probability of
completing repair. Fates are sampled with the **delayed** model: a lethally
damaged cell becomes *doomed*, keeps its site and is removed after a
phase-dependent delay. The **clonogenic** surviving fraction (alive and not
doomed) must agree with the mean survival probability.

```{julia}
#| label: survival

set_fate_model!(:delayed)
set_checkpoint!(:all)

for i in findall(alive0)            # survival without resetting the cells' clocks
    ph = cell_df.cell_cycle[i]
    gs = (ph == "G1" || ph == "G0") ? gsm2_cycle[1] : ph == "S" ? gsm2_cycle[2] : gsm2_cycle[3]
    cell_df.sp[i] = domain_GSM2(cell_df.dam_X_dom[i], cell_df.dam_Y_dom[i], gs)
end
SF_gsm2 = mean(cell_df.sp[alive0])
phase0  = copy(cell_df.cell_cycle)

compute_times_domain!(cell_df, gsm2_cycle; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = Inf, summary = true)
doomed0  = alive0 .& isfinite.(cell_df.death_time)
SF_clono = count(alive0 .& .!doomed0) / N_init
@printf("Mean GSM² survival %.3f; clonogenic surviving fraction %.3f\n", SF_gsm2, SF_clono)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-survival
#| fig-cap: "Left: survival probability as a function of depth. Right: as a function of the oxygen level (binned means). The hypoxic core is more resistant."

d   = cell_df[alive0, :]
gz  = sort(combine(groupby(d, :z), :sp => mean => :sp), :z)
d.Ob = round.(d.O; digits = 0)
gO  = sort(combine(groupby(d, :Ob), :sp => mean => :sp, nrow => :n), :Ob)
gO  = gO[gO.n .>= 5, :]

p1 = plot(gz.z, gz.sp; marker = :circle, ms = 3, color = :seagreen, label = "",
          xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "Mean survival probability", ylims = (0, 1))
p2 = plot(gO.Ob, gO.sp; marker = :circle, ms = 3, color = :steelblue, label = "",
          xlabel = "O₂ (%)", ylabel = "Mean survival probability", ylims = (0, 1))
plot(p1, p2; layout = (1, 2), size = (900, 380))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-fate
#| fig-cap: "Left: fraction of cells committed to death, by cell-cycle phase at irradiation. Right: time of radiation-induced death (density), by phase."

frac = [count(doomed0 .& (phase0 .== ph)) / max(count(alive0 .& (phase0 .== ph)), 1) for ph in PHASES]
p1 = bar(PHASES, frac; color = [PCOL[ph] for ph in PHASES], label = "",
         xlabel = "Phase at irradiation", ylabel = "Fraction committed to death", ylims = (0, 1))
p2 = plot(xlabel = "Time of death (h)", ylabel = "Probability density (h⁻¹)", legend = :topright)
for ph in PHASES
    t = cell_df.death_time[doomed0 .& (phase0 .== ph)]
    length(t) >= 10 && density!(p2, t; color = PCOL[ph], label = ph, trim = true)
end
plot(p1, p2; layout = (1, 2), size = (900, 380))
```

## Agent-based dynamics

The ABM runs one hour at a time, so that the total, clonogenic and doomed cells,
and the cell-cycle composition, are recorded every hour. Snapshots of the
spheroid are kept at selected times.

```{julia}
#| label: abm

rows  = DataFrame(t = Int[], total = Int[], clonogenic = Int[], doomed = Int[],
                  G0 = Int[], G1 = Int[], S = Int[], G2 = Int[], M = Int[])
snaps = Dict{Int, DataFrame}()

function record!(t)
    a  = cell_df.is_cell .== 1
    dm = a .& isfinite.(cell_df.death_time)
    cl = a .& .!dm
    push!(rows, (t, count(a), count(cl), count(dm),
                 [count(cl .& (cell_df.cell_cycle .== ph)) for ph in PHASES]...))
    t in SNAP_HOURS && (snaps[t] = DataFrame(x = cell_df.x[a], y = cell_df.y[a], z = cell_df.z[a],
                                            phase = String.(cell_df.cell_cycle[a]), doomed = dm[a]))
end

record!(0)
for h in 1:T_FOLLOW
    ts, _ = run_simulation_abm!(cell_df; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = 1.0,
                                snapshot_times = Int[], verbose = false,
                                return_dataframes = false, update_input = true)
    _advance_idle!(cell_df, 1.0 - (isempty(ts.time) ? 0.0 : ts.time[end]))
    record!(h)
end
last(rows, 3)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-population
#| fig-cap: "Left: total, clonogenic and doomed cells, normalized to the initial number. Right: cell-cycle composition of the clonogenic cells."

p1 = plot(rows.t, rows.total ./ N_init; color = :black, label = "total",
          xlabel = "Time after irradiation (h)", ylabel = "Cells / N₀", legend = :topleft)
plot!(p1, rows.t, rows.clonogenic ./ N_init; color = :seagreen, label = "clonogenic")
plot!(p1, rows.t, rows.doomed ./ N_init; color = :firebrick, ls = :dash, label = "doomed")
comp = hcat([rows[!, Symbol(ph)] for ph in PHASES]...) ./ max.(rows.clonogenic, 1)
p2 = areaplot(rows.t, comp; label = permutedims(PHASES), fillalpha = 0.85, lw = 0,
              seriescolor = permutedims([PCOL[ph] for ph in PHASES]), ylims = (0, 1),
              xlabel = "Time after irradiation (h)", ylabel = "Fraction of clonogenic cells",
              legend = :outerright)
plot(p1, p2; layout = (1, 2), size = (980, 380))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-snapshots
#| fig-cap: "Half spheroid (y ≥ 0) at 0, 24, 48 and 96 h after irradiation, coloured by cell-cycle phase; black: cells committed to death."

function half3d(s, t)
    k = s.y .>= cy
    p = plot(; xlabel = "x (µm)", ylabel = "y (µm)", zlabel = "z (µm)", legend = false,
             title = "$t h", titlefontsize = 10, camera = (-30, 20), aspect_ratio = :equal,
             left_margin = 2Plots.mm, bottom_margin = 2Plots.mm)
    for c in vcat(PHASES, "doomed")
        sel = k .& (c == "doomed" ? s.doomed : (.!s.doomed .& (s.phase .== c)))
        any(sel) && scatter!(p, s.x[sel], s.y[sel], s.z[sel]; ms = 2.5, msw = 0, color = PCOL[c])
    end
    p
end
plot([half3d(snaps[t], t) for t in SNAP_HOURS]...; layout = (1, 4), size = (1100, 330))
```

```{julia}
#| label: summary

i_min   = argmin(rows.total)
regrow  = findfirst(i -> i > i_min && rows.total[i] >= N_init, eachindex(rows.t))
@printf("Clonogenic surviving fraction:            %.3f\n", SF_clono)
@printf("Minimum of the total cell number:          %.0f%% of N₀ at %d h\n",
        100 * rows.total[i_min] / N_init, rows.t[i_min])
@printf("Total cells back to N₀:                    %s\n",
        regrow === nothing ? "not within $(T_FOLLOW) h" : "$(rows.t[regrow]) h")
@printf("Doomed cells still present at %d h:         %d\n", T_FOLLOW, rows.doomed[end])
```

## Where to go next {.unnumbered}

- Change `PARTICLE`, `E_MEAN`, `E_SIGMA` and `N_BINS` to explore other spectra;
  `N_BINS = 1` recovers a monoenergetic beam.
- Set `TRACK_SEG = true` to compare with the track-segment condition (all layers
  at the entrance energy).
- The scripts in `scripts/` reproduce the figures of the paper; see the README.
